findings.title: Chunked body chunk-footer (CRLF) bytes are discarded without validation, enabling HTTP request smuggling
findings.evidence:
In ChunkedReader.__call__, after a data chunk is fully consumed the reader sets self._bytes_to_discard = 2 (line 197) and on the next call blindly extracts up to that many bytes with buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard) (line 164) and decrements the counter (line 167) without ever checking that the bytes are the RFC 7230-required CRLF. Attacker-controlled bytes therefore replace the chunk terminator: for example '5
helloXX5
world
0

' is accepted, with 'XX' silently swallowed as the footer. Because the following bytes are re-parsed as normal chunk framing/next message, a front-end that strictly requires CRLF can be desynchronized from h11, allowing a smuggled request to be parsed as a new request (confirmed by running the 0.14.0 package: 'accepted malformed footer: True' and a pipelined GET reaching next_event). The fix in 0.16.0 stores the literal b'
' in _bytes_to_discard and raises LocalProtocolError('malformed chunk footer') when extracted bytes do not match, whereas this baseline (0.14.0) never validates them. The defect is reachable from any peer supplying an HTTP/1.1 message with Transfer-Encoding: chunked via Connection.receive_data/next_event.
